clue.text: Top dressing has been applied in the fowl-yard

definitions.text: Top dressing has been applied in the fowl-yard

parts.note: a cap is a dressing worn on top of the head
a garment that has been applied to the body is on

explanation.surface: A gardener or farmer spreads top dressing across the poultry yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole clue as a picture: a bird in the yard with a cap on, which is the castrated cockerel of the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a familiar bird of the poultry yard.

clue.text: Elizabeth accommodated by honey producer in Central America

indicators.note: something accommodated by another is housed within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the bee is the insect that makes honey
Liz is a short form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth is put up by a beekeeper somewhere in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodated by' means the girl's name is housed within the insect; 'in' before Central America is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies on the Caribbean coast of the Central American isthmus, south of Mexico.

clue.text: Darling, nothing is fully cooked

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
food that is fully cooked is done

explanation.surface: A cook reassures a sweetheart that nothing is quite ready yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are terms of endearment for a dearly cherished person.

clue.text: Lecture from the place where one lives

definitions.meaning: a formal speech delivered to an audience
the house number and street where someone resides

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal speech and the details of someone's residence.

clue.text: Bill meets Tom in France for a gossip

parts.note: a chit is a small bill or note of money owed
chat is the French word for cat, a tom being a male cat

explanation.surface: A man called Bill meets his friend Tom in France for a natter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Tom look like men's names; one is an account and the other a male cat, translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle light talk is another word for casual chatter.

clue.text: He works alone to import fish into Gaul

indicators.note: importing brings something inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: Gaul is the ancient name for the land that is now France
an eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A solitary trader sets out to bring fish into ancient Gaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to import' signals a container; 'He works alone' looks like a description of a hermit but defines an independent worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed person takes work independently rather than for one employer.

clue.text: To argue one needs to be articulate

definitions.meaning: a fluent speaker must possess vocabulary

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to quarrel, and literally a fluent speaker must possess vocabulary.

clue.text: Entrance made by church member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A grand doorway has been built by one of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway; it is the verb meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight and captivate them, as by enchantment.

clue.text: Fat man in exemplary turn-about

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
a turn-about faces the other way, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, introduces an exemplary case
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A stout man performs a model about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-about' and 'in' both act: 'exemplary' gives the abbreviation for 'for example', turned round, with the man placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarified butter used in Indian cooking is a cooking fat.

clue.text: Hector, being a man of action, holds explosive device

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts rather than talks
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Hector, a man of action, keeps a bomb to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a name; it is the verb meaning to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or boss others about overbearingly.

clue.text: Source of discontent if the electric blanket has been on

definitions.meaning: a place where trouble or unrest breeds

definitions.text: if the electric blanket has been on
definitions.meaning: a warmed mattress would be heated

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a breeding ground for unrest, and literally a warmed sleeping place.

clue.text: Original Stoic contributes nothing to Japanese philosophy

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism strongly associated with Japan
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The first Stoic thinker adds nothing to Japanese thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher of Citium founded the Stoic school in Athens.

clue.text: Interview a principal divine

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview or meet them
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A journalist interviews a senior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like a noun for a clergyman; it is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foresee or predict what is coming.

clue.text: Way a representative has obligation to submit tax

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
a duty is an obligation

explanation.surface: A politician is obliged to hand in a tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: STAMP DUTY is a British tax paid on buying property and on some documents.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British levy on property purchases and certain legal documents.

clue.text: Son conversed, yet carefully followed the game

parts.note: conversed means talked

explanation.surface: A son chatted while tracking the deer on a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters creep after their quarry stealthily, following game animals.

clue.text: Lots of beatings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a plentiful amount and also floggings with a whip.

clue.text: Magistrate is on the rocks

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served over nothing but frozen water, and a judge also carries this title

explanation.surface: A judge has hit hard times or is drinking spirits with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or magistrate is addressed by this title, and a drink on the rocks has only frozen water.

clue.text: Universal exercise in purchasing causes rebellion

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
purchase is leverage, and exercising it is levering or prising

explanation.surface: Universal shopping habits provoke a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchasing' looks like buying; purchase here means leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is a popular rising against authority.

clue.text: Where retailers have their goods reserved

definitions.meaning: on the premises of a shop

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means inside the shop and also kept waiting for the future.

clue.text: Failure to include old band of proselytisers

parts.note: a mission is a group sent out to convert people

explanation.surface: An old group of preachers failed to include everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out is the act of excluding it.

clue.text: Feature I encountered on returning

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: Someone notices a feature on getting back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on returning' applies only to 'encountered', which follows the I in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single feature or article in a list or newspaper is one entry.

clue.text: Stern way to raise the issue

definitions.meaning: the back end of a boat
bring up offspring, issue meaning children

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the back part, like a ship's stern, and also to bring up children.

clue.text: A Catholic woman who practises toxophily

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A Catholic woman takes up the bow and arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxophily is the sport of shooting with a bow, so one who practises it is a bowman.

clue.text: Analyse metal in a Roman coin, for instance

parts.note: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Testing the metal content of an old Roman coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine the purity of a metal or ore is to test it chemically.

clue.text: Wickedness of present times calls for guidance

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
vice is wickedness

explanation.surface: Modern immorality demands moral guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel or recommendation given to help someone decide is guidance.

clue.text: What Customs may do to create a legal precedent

definitions.meaning: border officers may examine a piece of luggage
a lawsuit whose outcome sets a principle for later ones

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is literally checking a suitcase, and also a lawsuit that sets a principle for later rulings.

clue.text: Theatre coach

definitions.meaning: the platform or profession of drama
a horse-drawn coach running between stations

explanation.definitionFit: The word means drama as a profession and also a stagecoach running between stops.

clue.text: No manager is replaced by Ulster Protestant

indicators.note: letters replaced into new positions signal a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A Protestant from Ulster takes over when no manager is in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal body strong in Northern Ireland (Ulster); its members bear this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Orange Order, the Protestant society of Northern Ireland.
